title: Pakistan, the Taliban and Khalilzad's claims
credits: Photos: Muhammad Amir / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Pakistan has rejected claims that it is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban.
The claims came from Zalmay Khalilzad, the former US envoy who negotiated America's deal with the Taliban.
On X, he said there were many reports that Pakistan was arming Afghans, and warned that ties could get much worse.
Pakistan's information ministry called them sweeping, baseless assertions.
It said they distract from the Taliban's responsibility to stop Afghan soil being used for attacks on Pakistan.
Islamabad pointed to UN monitoring reports on the presence of the TTP and Al-Qaeda in Afghanistan.
It also cited a US inspector general report estimating the TTP's strength at four to six thousand fighters.
The Taliban's spokesman, Zabiullah Mujahid, said Afghanistan has no interest in creating insecurity in Pakistan.
Pakistan demands that the Taliban end support for the TTP and the BLA, and says it remains open to engagement based on verifiable action.
Relations are tense. In September, Pakistan carried out airstrikes in the border region after attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Islamabad says it has repeatedly asked Kabul to dismantle militant sanctuaries.
